skill.name: hook
skill.description: Create, update, configure, and validate Claude Code hooks for local automation workflows.
skill.summary: Guides Claude Code hook creation, settings updates, validation, and review.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples or Markdown backticks rather than active malicious code. One static issue is confirmed because an example persists an API key in CLAUDE_ENV_FILE. Semantic review found high-impact hook automation risks but no prompt injection attempt.

remediation.issue: Generated hooks can create persistent automatic command execution.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before creating hook scripts or editing settings.local.json. Show the exact command, matcher, and event before enabling it.

remediation.issue: The environment example persists an API key in CLAUDE_ENV_FILE.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the API_KEY example with a non-secret variable. Add a warning to keep secrets out of hook scripts and environment files.

remediation.issue: Permission and prompt hooks can alter tool approval and model context.
remediation.suggestion: Forbid broad auto-approval by default. Require narrow matchers, explicit deny rules, and a clear review step for context-injecting hooks.

remediation.issue: Reference examples include abbreviated home and transcript paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use neutral placeholders and remind users not to hardcode personal paths, transcript files, or hidden user directories.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Hook Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The workflow creates or updates scripts in .claude/hooks and links them in settings.local.json. The reference also warns that hooks execute arbitrary shell commands and can access user-readable files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill directly instructs the agent to create hook scripts and update hook settings. The reference explicitly states these hooks execute arbitrary shell commands with user file access.

semantic_findings.title: Hook-Based Prompt and Permission Control
semantic_findings.description: The reference describes hooks that can approve tool use, modify inputs, block prompts, or add context. Generated hooks using these features can alter the agent workflow if misconfigured.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited sections define permission approval, input mutation, prompt blocking, and context injection behavior. These are documented features, but they create high-impact control points.

content.value_statement: Claude Code hooks are powerful but easy to misconfigure. This skill guides hook creation, configuration, validation, and security review.
actual_capabilities: Creates or updates hook scripts under .claude/hooks based on user requirements.
Links hooks in .claude/settings.local.json for selected Claude Code events.
Selects events such as PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, and SessionStart.
Adds validation, error handling, logging, and comments to generated hook scripts.
Tests hook syntax and execution behavior without creating test files.
Uses the included hooks reference to follow Claude Code hook schemas.
limitations: Hook scripts run with the user account permissions and can affect local files.
The skill does not provide sandboxing or enforce policy outside generated code.
Users must review commands before enabling hooks in shared or production workspaces.
Most procedures are Claude Code specific and may need adaptation for Codex workflows.

use_cases.title: Automate Project Checks
use_cases.description: Create hooks that run formatters, linters, or validation commands after file edits.

use_cases.title: Add Security Guardrails
use_cases.description: Build hooks that block unsafe shell commands, sensitive file access, or risky prompts.

use_cases.title: Configure Team Workflows
use_cases.description: Standardize local hook settings and reusable hook scripts across a project.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Hook
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one automation task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PostToolUse hook named format-after-edit. It should run our formatter after Write or Edit and report any safety checks.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing Hook
prompt_templates.scenario: Modify a hook while preserving working behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing hook named protect-main-branch. Add clearer error handling and keep the current branch protection behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Add Prompt Validation
prompt_templates.scenario: Block risky user prompts before processing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a UserPromptSubmit hook that blocks prompts containing secrets, tokens, or private keys. Explain how it is linked and tested.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Hook Policy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with multiple events and safeguards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hook policy for this repository using PreToolUse, PostToolUse, and Stop events. Include matchers, commands, risks, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Create a hook that warns when Bash uses slow search commands.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes a PreToolUse Bash hook, creates a validator script, links it to local settings, and reports the validation result.

output_examples.input: Add a hook that blocks prompts containing secrets.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a prompt validation workflow, explains the blocked patterns, updates the hook configuration, and lists manual review steps.

output_examples.input: Audit my existing hooks before I enable them.
output_examples.output: The skill reviews hook files and settings, highlights risky commands, checks syntax, and recommends safer matchers or confirmation steps.

best_practices: Review hook command paths and matchers before enabling them.
Keep hook scripts small, deterministic, and easy to test.
Store secrets outside generated hook code and avoid writing them to environment files.
anti_patterns: Enabling hooks that auto-approve broad file or shell access.
Hardcoding tokens, API keys, or private paths in hook scripts.
Using Stop hooks that can continue sessions without a termination guard.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates or updates Claude Code hook scripts and links them in local settings.

faq.question: Can it configure multiple hook events?
faq.answer: Yes. It can select events such as PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, and SessionStart.

faq.question: Does it run hooks in a sandbox?
faq.answer: No. Hooks run with normal user permissions, so every command needs review.

faq.question: Can it help with security checks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can add validation, deny rules, and checks for risky prompts or commands.

faq.question: Will it store credentials?
faq.answer: It should not store credentials. Users should keep secrets outside hook scripts and environment files.

faq.question: Is it only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: The workflow is designed for Claude Code hooks and may need changes for other tools.
